title: Experimental rollout resource cadence map & KPI notebook
body:
Purpose:
This is a working notebook for planning small-batch experimental rollouts (aka feature-sculpting) that explicitly ties traffic ramp steps to resource cadence, instrumentation, and KPI gates. Use when we want to test behavior & unit-economics before a full phased launch.

Executive summary:
- Goal: Validate product hypothesis for the new streaming-chat prompt-simplifier and confirm no material SLO regressions or cost blowouts across the first 50k daily active requests.
- Primary success signal: sustained user success rate >= 92% (end-to-end), p95 latency for inference < 450ms, and incremental cost per 1k requests <= $1.85 after caching/kv optimizations.
- Rollout style: quota-based canary (daily traffic windowing) with explicit resource buffer and autoscaler holdback periods.

Key KPIs (measurement & targets):
- Availability (platform): target >= 99.95% (measured by request success, 5m windows)
- Model latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 450ms (inference time excluding network)
- Error rate: total request error rate < 0.8% (includes model failures, timeouts, validation rejects)
- Quality proxy: success_rate (task-specific pass) >= 92% on curated prompt set (A/B test vs baseline)
- Cost: incremental cost per 1k requests <= $1.85 (after batching & cache) and monthly burn delta <= 12% in pilot phase
- Operator load: incidents requiring human intervention <= 1 per week during canary windows
- Regression alerts: any hallucination-rate delta > 2.5pp triggers rollout pause

Resource cadence map (high-level timeline):
Week 0 (prep, owner: PM + Infra):
  - Finalize canary traffic windows and quota policy (daily 2-hour window)
  - Baseline capacity plan: reserve 30% extra GPU pool capacity for first 48h of ramp
  - Instrumentation: ensure model-level traces, token-level cost sampling, KV cache hit-rate metric, and request-id propagation to logs
  - Smoke test matrix and script written (see section 'Smoke tests')

Week 1 (small-batch canary, owner: product-ops + SRE):
  - Traffic: 1% of baseline traffic routed into canary window (2h/day) for 3 consecutive days
  - Capacity: autoscaler holdback set to not scale beyond 60% of burst without manual approval
  - Monitoring: dashboards live, PCR (post-candidate report) template populated after day 3
  - Decision gate: proceed if error_rate < 0.6% and p95 latency < 350ms and cost per 1k < $2.10

Week 2 (expanded canary, owner: product + infra):
  - Traffic: 5% traffic across two 2-hour windows (morning and evening), 5 days
  - Capacity: reduce reserve to 20% as autoscaler behavior observed; enable ephemeral extra nodes for controlled burst tests
  - Experiment: enable intelligent batching profile (size cap 16), KV prefix cache enabled for common prompts
  - Decision gate: proceed if quality proxy delta <= 1.5pp and operational errors stable

Week 3 (broader ramp, owner: PM + product-ops):
  - Traffic: 20% steady daytime traffic for 7 days
  - Capacity: normal autoscale; observe spot/ondemand mix for Dedicated pools; cost forecast updated daily
  - Decision gate: proceed to 50% if all KPIs within thresholds for >=72h

Rollout ramp schedule (percentage & guardrails):
  - 1% -> 5% (min 3 days each) -> 20% (min 7 days) -> 50% (min 5 days) -> 100%
  - Forced rollback rule: any single 1h window with error_rate > 2.0% OR p95 latency > 700ms -> immediate abort and redirect to baseline model
  - Manual pause rule: hallucination-rate increase > 2.5pp OR cost-per-1k exceeding threshold by >15% for 48h

Cost model snapshot (pilot):
  - Baseline assumptions: avg tokens per request = 420, batch efficiency improvement expected +18% after batching tuning
  - Unit costs used: GPU-inference-hour $4.80, baseline model compute per 1k reqs = 0.13 GPU-hr -> baseline compute cost $0.624/1k; network+infra overhead ~ $0.45/1k -> total baseline ~$1.07/1k
  - Pilot delta estimates: additional model complexity increases compute by +30% before quantization -> pre-optimization cost = $1.39/1k; expected optimizations reduce to target <= $1.85/1k total including infra
  - Contingency: budget cap for pilot $15k; alert when cumulative pilot spend reaches 70%

Smoke tests (must pass before any traffic ramp):
  - End-to-end: sample 100 canonical prompts through routing stack; assert 95% success, latency p95 < 480ms
  - Canary-specific: validate KV cache warm path for top 20 prompts; expected cache hit-rate >= 60% within 30 minutes of window start
  - Failure mode: simulate GPU OOM and ensure fallback to smaller quantized model within 90s and that fallback does not increase hallucination_rate by >1.5pp
  - Observability: logs include request_id, model_version, cache_status, tokens_out, and sampled diff against baseline response (for quality telemetry)

Preflight readiness checklist (owner and sign-off matrix):
  - Instrumentation: metrics & traces deployed (owner: infra) -> sign-off: Ruth Goldberg
  - Dashboards: rollout dashboard + KPI tiles (owner: product-ops) -> sign-off: Owen Patel
  - Playbooks: rollback & on-call runbook published (owner: SRE) -> sign-off: Samir Joshi
  - Contract & privacy review completed (owner: legal) -> sign-off: Claudia Rivera (legal)
  - Customer comms template drafted (owner: comms) -> sign-off: Derek Nguyen

KPI monitoring & alert thresholds (practical):
  - Pager alert: request error rate (5m) > 1.5% for 10m -> P1 (eng-sre)
  - Slack alert: p95 latency > 600ms for 10m -> P2 (product-ops)
  - Ticket alert: daily cost overrun > 20% vs forecast -> Ops review (finance + product)
  - Silent telemetry: hallucination delta measured daily; only on-call escalates when delta > 2.5pp

Data collection & analysis plan:
  - Sampling: capture 1 in 10 responses for quality diffing vs baseline; store diffs in ephemeral evaluation bucket for 30d
  - Evaluation harness: run daily batch eval on curated prompt set (200 prompts) and report pass/fail by KPI
  - Attribution: use phased tags (canary-1, canary-5, canary-20) to join telemetry with billing and user metrics

Contingency playbook (top 3 immediate actions):
  1) If error spike: switch traffic back to baseline variant and strip canary routing rules; kill any new model-serving jobs and roll to previous image
  2) If cost blowout: pause canary windows and throttle by quota; disable nonessential telemetry sampling for short-term relief
  3) If quality regression: pause and trigger overnight root-cause (sample diffs, compare gradients of model outputs, escalate to ML ops)

Owner RACI (short):
  - Product Manager (Marina Chen): accountable for go/no-go, KPI targets, customer comms
  - Product-Ops (Owen Patel): responsible for daily monitoring, PCR docs, dashboard maintenance
  - SRE (Samir Joshi): responsible for autoscale config, failover rules, runbooks
  - Infrastructure (Ruth Goldberg): responsible for model infra provisioning, capacity reservations
  - Legal & Security (Claudia Rivera): consulted for compliance and data handling

Notes & open questions (working):
  - Should we allow short 15m micro-windows for early morning peak validation? (pros: faster signal; cons: noisy telemetry)
  - Need clearer guidance on how cache-warm durations scale by region — add regional cache heatmap in next iteration
  - Investigate cost-optimization: per-model quantization + auto-eviction policy for inactive KV prefixes

Next steps & action items:
  - (Marina) Book cross-functional readiness review for 2025-01-17
  - (Ruth) Deploy tracing patch and confirm token-level cost sampling by EOD 2025-01-14
  - (Owen) Create rollout dashboard and PCR template, link to GitHub PR for scripts
  - (Samir) Draft emergency rollback checklist and run a tabletop drill with on-call rotation

Appendix: quick PCR (post-candidate report) template fields:
  - window_date, traffic_fraction, avg_tokens, p50_latency, p95_latency, error_rate, cache_hit_rate, unit_cost_per_1k, hallucination_delta_pp, operator_incidents, decision (proceed/pause/rollback), notes

End of notebook. This doc is intentionally iterative — treat as working source of truth for experimental rollouts until marked final.
